requirements.original: testcasename() return charstring
requirements.canonical: The `testcasename` function has the signature `testcasename() return charstring`, with no formal parameters and a return value of type `charstring`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- testcasename() return charstring

requirements.original: The testcasename function shall return the unqualified name of the actually executing test case.
requirements.canonical: The `testcasename` function SHALL return the unqualified name of the currently executing test case, also when called by a parallel test component.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- The testcasename function shall return the unqualified name of the actually executing test case.

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-8; initial octet sequence: EF BB BF; comments: signature not required / no effect
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-8 coding scheme IS EF BB BF.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-8; initial octet sequence: EF BB BF; comments: signature not required / no effect

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-8; initial octet sequence: EF BB BF; comments: signature not required / no effect
requirements.canonical: For UTF-8, the initial octet sequence (BOM) is not required and IS of no effect as a signature.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-8; initial octet sequence: EF BB BF; comments: signature not required / no effect

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16BE; initial octet sequence: FE FF; comments: no signature meaning
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-16BE coding scheme IS FE FF.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-16BE; initial octet sequence: FE FF; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16BE; initial octet sequence: FE FF; comments: no signature meaning
requirements.canonical: For UTF-16BE, the octet sequence FE FF IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).

ambiguity.issue: 'no signature meaning' does not say whether FE FF at the start of UTF-16BE data is treated as a ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE character (and therefore kept by `remove_bom`) or is still removed as a BOM; the first reading was chosen as it follows Unicode practice.
readings: For UTF-16BE, a leading FE FF IS NOT a BOM, and `remove_bom` IS NOT required to remove it.
For UTF-16BE, a leading FE FF IS a BOM that does not identify the coding scheme, and `remove_bom` removes it.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-16BE; initial octet sequence: FE FF; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE; comments: no signature meaning
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-16LE coding scheme IS FF FE.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-16LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE; comments: no signature meaning
requirements.canonical: For UTF-16LE, the octet sequence FF FE IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).

ambiguity.issue: 'no signature meaning' does not say whether FF FE at the start of UTF-16LE data is treated as a ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE character (and therefore kept by `remove_bom`) or is still removed as a BOM; the first reading was chosen as it follows Unicode practice.
readings: For UTF-16LE, a leading FF FE IS NOT a BOM, and `remove_bom` IS NOT required to remove it.
For UTF-16LE, a leading FF FE IS a BOM that does not identify the coding scheme, and `remove_bom` removes it.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-16LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16; initial octet sequence: FE FF FF FE; comments: signature (default FE FF)
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-16 coding scheme IS FE FF or FF FE.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-16; initial octet sequence: FE FF FF FE; comments: signature (default FE FF)

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-16; initial octet sequence: FE FF FF FE; comments: signature (default FE FF)
requirements.canonical: For UTF-16, the initial octet sequence IS a signature, and FE FF IS the default initial octet sequence.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-16; initial octet sequence: FE FF FF FE; comments: signature (default FE FF)

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32BE; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF; comments: no signature meaning
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-32BE coding scheme IS 00 00 FE FF.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-32BE; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32BE; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF; comments: no signature meaning
requirements.canonical: For UTF-32BE, the octet sequence 00 00 FE FF IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).

ambiguity.issue: 'no signature meaning' does not say whether 00 00 FE FF at the start of UTF-32BE data is treated as a ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE character (and therefore kept by `remove_bom`) or is still removed as a BOM; the first reading was chosen as it follows Unicode practice.
readings: For UTF-32BE, a leading 00 00 FE FF IS NOT a BOM, and `remove_bom` IS NOT required to remove it.
For UTF-32BE, a leading 00 00 FE FF IS a BOM that does not identify the coding scheme, and `remove_bom` removes it.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-32BE; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE 00 00; comments: no signature meaning
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-32LE coding scheme IS FF FE 00 00.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-32LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE 00 00; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE 00 00; comments: no signature meaning
requirements.canonical: For UTF-32LE, the octet sequence FF FE 00 00 IS NOT a signature (it has no signature meaning).

ambiguity.issue: 'no signature meaning' does not say whether FF FE 00 00 at the start of UTF-32LE data is treated as a ZERO WIDTH NO-BREAK SPACE character (and therefore kept by `remove_bom`) or is still removed as a BOM; the first reading was chosen as it follows Unicode practice.
readings: For UTF-32LE, a leading FF FE 00 00 IS NOT a BOM, and `remove_bom` IS NOT required to remove it.
For UTF-32LE, a leading FF FE 00 00 IS a BOM that does not identify the coding scheme, and `remove_bom` removes it.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-32LE; initial octet sequence: FF FE 00 00; comments: no signature meaning

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF FF FE 00 00; comments: signature (default 00 00 FE FF)
requirements.canonical: The initial octet sequence (byte order mark, BOM) of the UTF-32 coding scheme IS 00 00 FE FF or FF FE 00 00.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-32; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF FF FE 00 00; comments: signature (default 00 00 FE FF)

requirements.original: Coding scheme: UTF-32; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF FF FE 00 00; comments: signature (default 00 00 FE FF)
requirements.canonical: For UTF-32, the initial octet sequence IS a signature, and 00 00 FE FF IS the default initial octet sequence.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- Coding scheme: UTF-32; initial octet sequence: 00 00 FE FF FF FE 00 00; comments: signature (default 00 00 FE FF)

requirements.original: When the function testcasename is called if the control part is being executed but no testcase, it shall return the empty string.
requirements.canonical: When `testcasename` is called while the module control function is executing and no test case is executing, `testcasename` SHALL return the empty string.
requirements.condition: the module control function is executing and no test case is executing

ambiguity.issue: Uses the outdated term 'control part'; V4.17.1 uses 'module control function'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- When the function testcasename is called if the control part is being executed but no testcase, it shall return the empty string.

requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of predefined functions defined in clause 16.1.2 apply to `testcasename`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.2 -- The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.original: hostid(in charstring idkind := "Ipv4orIPv6") return charstring
requirements.canonical: The `hostid` function has the signature `hostid(in charstring idkind := "Ipv4orIPv6") return charstring`, with an `in` formal parameter `idkind` of type `charstring` and a return value of type `charstring`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.3 -- hostid(in charstring idkind := "Ipv4orIPv6") return charstring

requirements.original: hostid(in charstring idkind := "Ipv4orIPv6") return charstring
requirements.canonical: If `hostid` is called without an actual parameter, the `idkind` formal parameter IS "Ipv4orIPv6" by default.
requirements.condition: no actual parameter is given for idkind
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.3 -- hostid(in charstring idkind := "Ipv4orIPv6") return charstring

requirements.original: The hostid function shall return the host id of the test component or module control executing the hostid function in form of a character string.
requirements.canonical: The `hostid` function SHALL return, as a `charstring`, the host id of the test component or module control function executing the `hostid` function.

ambiguity.issue: 'host id' is not defined; for a host with several addresses of the requested kind it is not stated which one is returned. The reading 'any one address of the executing host' was chosen.
readings: The `hostid` function SHALL return any one address of the requested kind of the host executing the calling component.
The `hostid` function SHALL return the address under which the executing host was addressed (e.g. the host given in `execute`).

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.3 -- The hostid function shall return the host id of the test component or module control executing the hostid function in form of a character string.

requirements.original: The in parameter idkind allows to specify the expected id format to be returned.
requirements.canonical: The `idkind` formal parameter of `hostid` specifies the expected format of the returned host id.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.3 -- The in parameter idkind allows to specify the expected id format to be returned.

requirements.original: Predefined idkind values are:
requirements.canonical: The predefined values of the `idkind` formal parameter of `hostid` ARE "Ipv4orIPv6", "Ipv4" and "Ipv6".

ambiguity.issue: 'Predefined' suggests that other idkind values may exist, but it is not stated whether other values are tool-specific extensions, yield the empty string, or cause an error. The reading 'other values are implementation-defined' was chosen.
readings: Values of `idkind` other than the predefined ones MAY be supported by a tool with implementation-defined meaning.
Values of `idkind` other than the predefined ones SHALL cause `hostid` to return the empty string.
Values of `idkind` other than the predefined ones SHALL cause an error.

requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.3 -- Predefined idkind values are:

requirements.original: The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.
requirements.canonical: The general error causes of predefined functions defined in clause 16.1.2 apply to `hostid`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: C.6.3 -- The general error causes in clause 16.1.2 apply.

requirements.original: A preprocessing macro is a macro that is replaced by a preprocessor or a compiler with a charstring or integer value respectively before compilation.
requirements.canonical: A preprocessing macro IS a macro that a preprocessor or compiler replaces with a charstring or integer value before compilation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.0 -- A preprocessing macro is a macro that is replaced by a preprocessor or a compiler with a charstring or integer value respectively before compilation.

requirements.original: Preprocessing macros shall not be replaced inside literal charstring values and templates and not in TTCN-3 comments.
requirements.canonical: A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a literal charstring value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.0 -- Preprocessing macros shall not be replaced inside literal charstring values and templates and not in TTCN-3 comments.

requirements.original: Preprocessing macros shall not be replaced inside literal charstring values and templates and not in TTCN-3 comments.
requirements.canonical: A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a literal charstring template (e.g. a pattern string).

ambiguity.issue: "templates" is ambiguous: D.5 examples (D.5-s014) show __SCOPE__ being replaced in template definitions, so "templates" most likely means literal character string templates such as pattern strings. The canonical text chooses that reading.
readings: A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a literal charstring template such as a pattern string.
A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced anywhere inside a template definition.

requirements.header: // @requirement: D.0 -- Preprocessing macros shall not be replaced inside literal charstring values and templates and not in TTCN-3 comments.

requirements.original: Preprocessing macros shall not be replaced inside literal charstring values and templates and not in TTCN-3 comments.
requirements.canonical: A preprocessing macro SHALL NOT be replaced inside a TTCN-3 comment.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.0 -- Preprocessing macros shall not be replaced inside literal charstring values and templates and not in TTCN-3 comments.

requirements.original: In the TTCN-3 code, it can be used like a charstring or an integer value respectively.
requirements.canonical: A preprocessing macro MAY be used in TTCN-3 code wherever a charstring or integer value, respectively, can be used.

examples.text:
const charstring c_myConst:= __FILE__;
  //c_myConst is for example "/home/myhome/MyTest.ttcn"

const charstring c_myConst:= __BFILE__;
  // c_myConst is for example "MyTest.ttcn"

requirements.header: // @requirement: D.0 -- In the TTCN-3 code, it can be used like a charstring or an integer value respectively.

requirements.original: The __MODULE__ preprocessing macro denotes the module name in which the macro is used.
requirements.canonical: The `__MODULE__` preprocessing macro denotes the name of the module in which the macro is used.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.1 -- The __MODULE__ preprocessing macro denotes the module name in which the macro is used.

requirements.original: A preprocessor or compiler shall replace all occurrences of __MODULE__ with the actual module name in form of a charstring value.
requirements.canonical: A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__MODULE__` with the actual module name as a charstring value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.1 -- A preprocessor or compiler shall replace all occurrences of __MODULE__ with the actual module name in form of a charstring value.

requirements.original: The __FILE__ preprocessing macro denotes the canonical (absolute) file name, i.e. the full path and the basic file name, in which the macro is used.
requirements.canonical: The `__FILE__` preprocessing macro denotes the canonical (absolute) file name, i.e. the full path and the basic file name, of the file in which the macro is used.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.2 -- The __FILE__ preprocessing macro denotes the canonical (absolute) file name, i.e. the full path and the basic file name, in which the macro is used.

requirements.original: A preprocessor or compiler shall replace all occurrences of __FILE__ with the actual canonical (absolute) file name in form of a charstring value.
requirements.canonical: A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__FILE__` with the actual canonical (absolute) file name as a charstring value.

examples.text:
const charstring c_myConst:= __FILE__;
  //c_myConst is for example "/home/myhome/MyTest.ttcn"

requirements.header: // @requirement: D.2 -- A preprocessor or compiler shall replace all occurrences of __FILE__ with the actual canonical (absolute) file name in form of a charstring value.

requirements.original: The __BFILE__ preprocessing macro denotes the basic (relative) file name, i.e. without path, in which the macro is used.
requirements.canonical: The `__BFILE__` preprocessing macro denotes the basic (relative) file name, i.e. without path, of the file in which the macro is used.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.3 -- The __BFILE__ preprocessing macro denotes the basic (relative) file name, i.e. without path, in which the macro is used.

requirements.original: A preprocessor or compiler shall replace all occurrences of __BFILE__ with the actual basic (relative) file name in form of a charstring value.
requirements.canonical: A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace every occurrence of `__BFILE__` with the actual basic (relative) file name as a charstring value.

examples.text:
const charstring c_myConst:= __BFILE__;
  // c_myConst is for example "MyTest.ttcn"

requirements.header: // @requirement: D.3 -- A preprocessor or compiler shall replace all occurrences of __BFILE__ with the actual basic (relative) file name in form of a charstring value.

requirements.original: The __LINE__ preprocessing macro denotes the line number of the file in which the macro is used.
requirements.canonical: The `__LINE__` preprocessing macro denotes the line number, in the file, of the line in which the macro is used.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.4 -- The __LINE__ preprocessing macro denotes the line number of the file in which the macro is used.

requirements.original: A preprocessor or compiler shall replace each occurrence of __LINE__ with the actual line number in form of an integer value.
requirements.canonical: A preprocessor or compiler SHALL replace each occurrence of `__LINE__` with the actual line number as an integer value.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.4 -- A preprocessor or compiler shall replace each occurrence of __LINE__ with the actual line number in form of an integer value.

requirements.original: A file starts with line number 1.
requirements.canonical: The first line of a file IS line number 1.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.4 -- A file starts with line number 1.

requirements.original: Each newline shall increase the line number by 1 (see clause A.1.5.1).
requirements.canonical: Each newline SHALL increase the line number by 1.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.4 -- Each newline shall increase the line number by 1 (see clause A.1.5.1).

requirements.original: Also newlines of commented lines shall increase the line number by 1.
requirements.canonical: A newline inside a commented line SHALL also increase the line number by 1.
requirements.header: // @requirement: D.4 -- Also newlines of commented lines shall increase the line number by 1.
